verses.text: Yahweh told Moses:
“Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use them to call the community together and to signal when the camps should move out. 🎺
When both trumpets sound, the whole community will gather in front of you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
When only one sounds, the leaders who head Israel’s thousands will gather in front of you.
When you sound the alarm, the camps on the east side will move out.
Sound it a second time, and the camps on the south side will move out. Use the alarm to signal that it’s time to travel.
When you’re calling the assembly together, blow the trumpets without sounding the alarm.
“Aaron’s sons, the priests, will blow the trumpets. That rule stands for every generation.
When you go into battle in your own land against an enemy who’s oppressing you, sound the alarm with the trumpets. Yahweh your God will remember you and save you from your enemies.

“On your days of celebration, at your appointed festivals, and at the start of each month, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings. They’ll serve as a reminder for you before your God. I’m Yahweh your God.”
In the second year, on day twenty of the second month, the cloud lifted from over the tabernacle of the covenant.
The Israelites moved out from the Sinai wilderness in stages, and the cloud came to rest in the wilderness of Paran.
That was the first time they moved out at Yahweh’s command through Moses.
Judah’s camp moved out first under its standard, division by division. Nahshon son of Amminadab led Judah’s fighting men.
Nethanel son of Zuar led the fighting men from Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon led the fighting men from Zebulun.
The tabernacle was taken down, and Gershon’s and Merari’s descendants moved out carrying it.
Next came Reuben’s camp, marching under its standard, division by division. Elizur son of Shedeur led Reuben’s fighting men.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai led the fighting men from Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Deuel led the fighting men from Gad.
The Kohathites moved out carrying the holy things. The others set up the tabernacle before they arrived.
Ephraim’s camp moved out under its standard, division by division. Elishama son of Ammihud led Ephraim’s fighting men.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur led the fighting men from Manasseh.
Abidan son of Gideoni led the fighting men from Benjamin.
Dan’s camp moved out under its standard, division by division, guarding the rear of all the camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai led Dan’s fighting men.
Pagiel son of Ochran led the fighting men from Asher.
Ahira son of Enan led the fighting men from Naphtali.
That’s the order the Israelites traveled in, division by division, when they moved out.

Moses told Hobab, son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We’re headed to the place Yahweh said he’d give us. Come with us and we’ll treat you well, because Yahweh has promised good things for Israel.”
Hobab replied, “I’m going back to my own land and my own family. I’m not coming with you.”
Moses said, “Please don’t leave us. You know where we can camp out in the wilderness. You can be our eyes out there.
Come with us, and whatever good Yahweh does for us, we’ll do the same for you.”
They traveled three days from Yahweh’s mountain. The ark of Yahweh’s covenant went ahead of them on that three-day journey to find a place for them to rest.
Yahweh’s cloud was over them by day as they moved out from camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, Yahweh! Scatter your enemies! Let those who hate you run from you!”
And whenever it came to rest, he would say, “Come back, Yahweh, to the countless thousands of Israel.”
